tests_read.why: Asks floor-machine.mjs nextFloor on a fixed Objection and its Rebuttal: the target moves, mode, holder, start, seconds and stack stay, one card is handed, and five refusals are compared one by one; it would fail if the row restarted the clock or moved in a debate. Its last assertion only reads that three keys exist in both language files.
Asks repointRefusal with handed-in participants and absentees on both modes and barRefusal for the bar's button; a pure judgement, so it does not show what the GM is told (see E110-1).
Asks floorSpeakers on 17 floors and holds each answer to modeAllows(floor, 'speak'); pure.

Asks floorHold over handed facts (listener, speaker, pair, debate, outside the trial, no list yet) and reads both lines' placeholders; its last assertion is a source read that registerTrialVoices names the trialQueue setting.

The Scrum rows, roundNextId and turnFooter are asked as pure calls and would fail; 'the vote's opening ends any floor' is held here by a regex over vote.mjs openRound and a typeof - the behaviour is tier 2 E110-T3's, to join.
Asks trialMusicState on 11 floors with every own state mapped and with none; pure. It does not read the order of MUSIC_STATES, so it cannot see E110-4.

Drives handleTrialGm and repointOnPrimary on the primary against a real card and receipt and compares the floor, the card's flags and line, the receipt, the clock and the count of public cards per press; needs three students with a connected player (the harness has three).

Counts updateUser writes and reads each player's permission and the store through an Objection, a Rebuttal, the end, a Monocub, a Panic turn, a crash and a release. Its optional fourth player M is expected 'open' although M is a Monocub from the start: with four such players the expectation contradicts D-E110-A (finding E110-3); with the harness's three players that branch does not run.
From the players' own pages: the permissions on the primary, the line each player reads, the redirect's floor and public card on every page, the Rebuttal's pair, the end and an empty store.

findings.failure_scenario: A GM opens Re-point during an Objection (the dialog preselects the current target, trial.mjs:1543-1544) and presses Re-point without changing it: nothing is written, and the notice says 'You cannot do that right now.' instead of 'The Objection is already aimed at that student.' The notes (line 14) say each has its own line.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a dynamic key build (DRPG.Floor. + variable), for a reader of floorStep's refusal, for barRefusal answering the two keys (it answers only noExchange for repoint, trial-floor.mjs:1437) and for a tooltip that carries them: none. The absent case cannot be chosen in the dialog (it lists connected participants only), so only the same-target line is reachable from the window; both are reachable from the API.

findings.title: The claim text of floor.repoint still says 'connected or not' for the target
findings.what_happens: The row's claims line reads 'one of the trial's participants (vote.mjs trialParticipants, connected or not; E51 C6)'. Since E110 C1 the primary refuses a target whose player is not connected (trial-floor.mjs:1261) and the dialog lists connected participants only (trial.mjs:1530).
findings.failure_scenario: A reader of the bridge's table who relies on the claim line to know who judges targetId reads a rule the code no longer has; the census row in tests-tier0.mjs:9360 was brought to repointRefusal, the claim line was not.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked whether absentOf could answer nothing on the primary (it reads the connected users) and whether the claim is quoted by a test that would pin the old words: R1b reads that a claim exists for the id, not its words.

findings.title: E110-T2 expects its optional fourth player, a Monocub from the start, to stay open through an Objection
findings.what_happens: With four or more connected players whose only voice is a living student the test makes the fourth, M, a Monocub before the trial and expects 'open' for M in every step (const m = M ? ['open'] : []). The settle blocks a Monocub the floor does not name (voice.mjs:1803-1806; D-E110-A), as the same test expects of H in its own 'monocub' step ([2, [open, blocked, blocked]]).
findings.failure_scenario: Tier 2 run in a world with four connected players each owning one living student: the Objection step reads 2 writes and M 'blocked', the expectation says 1 and 'open', and the test goes red on a module that is right. The harness and the gate's sandbox have three players, so the branch has not run.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that M is not on the trial's list (deadForTrial leaves Monocubs out), that M's account has no other character (the pick requires the student to be the account's only voice) and that 08048db0 changed only the H step of the expectation.

findings.title: With a playlist mapped to the vote, a debate or an Objection opened after the vote's first opening plays the vote's music
findings.what_happens: voteMusicPlays is true from the vote's first opening in the trial until the verdict (voteOpenedAt is kept by a restart and cleared only at the next trial's entry). In MUSIC_STATES the vote's row stands after the modes' own rows and before trial.objection and trial.debate, and currentState takes the first row whose test holds. Nothing refuses a floor after the vote opened (only the Closing's Resume does, floor-machine.mjs:290).
findings.failure_scenario: The GM maps a playlist to The vote and none to the Rebuttal. The vote ends in a tie, the table argues on and the GM opens the debate again; a player objects. The vote's playlist plays through the debate and through the Objection's minute, while a Testimony with its own playlist mapped would switch. The notes (line 54) say Nonstop Debate and the Objection keep the states they had.
findings.refutation_tried: Q-E110-14's answer is 'from the vote's opening (or its count) to the verdict', so by its letter the vote's music through a reopened debate is the rule taken; what remains is that the modes' own rows win over the vote and the two older rows lose to it, which the comment at music-states.mjs:191-194 does not foresee ('the vote ends every floor, so no mode's row competes with it'). Not driven: the harness reads the state, and no test opens a floor after a vote.

stages.grade_reasons: Every promise of the notes is in the code of 1.2.118 and the main ones are driven, not only read: tier 1 R7100-R7110 are green in the base run (tier01.log lines 1773-1785), tier 2 E110-T1..T4 and scenarios 67 V, 33 A23 and 30 drive the redirect and the muting on the primary and on the players' pages (their base results to join). Held down by: the main promise's last link - a microphone that really stops and comes back without a reload - rests on LIVE-E110-01, and none of the five LIVE-E110 items has a recorded reading (0 hits in both live-readings files); two parts are held by reading alone and say so (a disconnected Scrum speaker, the thesis window); four nits found, one of them a line of the notes that does not hold as written (E110-1). Three defects of this stage were repaired by E59 one release later (the vote's music watch B-S1, the Panic Round's double sound B-T8, the handbooks B-T5 and B-S2), so they do not count against 1.2.118.

findings.title: The held Key fee card's button charges whatever chapter the clock is in when it is pressed
findings.where: scripts/key-remnants.mjs:683-735 (chargeForUnfoundKeys: no phase read), :790-801 (wireChargeHeld: wired by the card's flag alone); scripts/gm-bridge.mjs:137-141 (wired on every render of the card); scripts/trial-progress.mjs:347 and :604-606 (keysCharged is the chapter's and survives the trial's entry)
findings.what_happens: Until E109 the charge was asked only as the clock entered a Class Trial (clock.mjs:1108-1111) or from a console. The card E109 gave a button stays in the chat log; every render on a GM's browser wires the button again ('a reload draws it again'), and a press runs chargeForUnfoundKeys for the clock's chapter. Its guards are the chapter's stamp and 'too late' (a closed earlier case and no case in the clock's chapter); neither asks whether a trial is running or whether the card is this chapter's.
findings.failure_scenario: Chapter 1's trial opens while a Truth Bullet lacks its answer key on the primary: the held card appears. In chapter 2 a body is found and the investigation runs (caseKeyCount(2) is a number). A GM scrolling the log presses 'Charge the Key fee' on the chapter-1 card: the fee is counted on the Keys found so far (none yet: 3 Despair a Key to each Monokuma for the whole bar), keysCharged is stamped for chapter 2 and the Reveal's paid count written, so the honest charge at chapter 2's trial entry is skipped and Keys found afterwards are still paid for.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a phase check in chargeForUnfoundKeys, in handleKeysCharge (bridge-runs-records.mjs:736-739) and in the keys.charge row (bridge-table.mjs:1154-1160: gmOnly only); for a chapter on the card's flag (keyChargeHeld: true alone); for the chapter's end deleting the card (only a season reset clears the chat). With no case in the new chapter the press is refused as too late, so the window is from the new chapter's incident to its trial entry. Not driven: R7130 reads source text.

findings.title: One window text and two player handbook lines still call the Tamper stage 'the clean-up'
findings.what_happens: The murder window's note for a death by one's own hand ends 'the incident goes straight to the clean-up'; the handbook says 'goes straight to the clean-up' and 'an incident that reached the clean-up closes'. The tracker and five cards say Tamper.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM setting up a death by one's own hand reads 'the clean-up' in the window and 'Tamper' on the tracker a moment later for the same stage.
findings.refutation_tried: Q-E109-1 keeps the attempts' words ('a clean-up attempt', 'clean-up roll', the Cleaning Tool); these three name the stage the incident goes to, not an attempt. The notes declare the handbook lines as not read one by one (line 217-218); the UI text is not declared, and R7120's list of cards leaves it out.

findings.title: The reset's 'actions' label does not name everything the group clears
findings.what_happens: The label lists rests, barricades, Bounties, Confusions, room effects, masks, tails, watches, eavesdrops, lock picks, crossings and the rolls' records. The group also cuts who used which facility, the bedroom notes waiting for their owners, the Monocubs' move counts and, since E112, the opening's veils; the list of sheet writes (sheetWrites, the audit's rows) is in the group too and is named only if 'the rolls' records' is read to cover it.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM who unticks 'actions' to keep, say, the Monocubs' caps or a waiting bedroom note cannot learn from the window that the group holds them.
findings.refutation_tried: Counted the group's stores at v1.2.115 (18) and today (19) by script; 'the rests' is the cast's own count, not the facilityUses store. The four are bookkeeping a GM rarely thinks of, which is why this is a nit and not more.

findings.title: With the files open to players an existing copy is not read at load, and the notes say only that nothing is written
findings.where: scripts/case-copy.mjs:261-268 (copyAtLoad returns before readServerCopies when filesPrivate() answers a reason)
findings.what_happens: The notes: 'Every GM's browser reads it when it opens the world'; 'otherwise it writes nothing'. The code also skips the read, and with it the 'empty here' notice; a GM who is not the primary is told nothing at all at load.
findings.failure_scenario: A copy was written in earlier sessions; the switch is turned off (or a player's account is given FILES_BROWSE). The owner opens the world alone on the second computer: the planner is empty although the file is on the server, and the only word is the primary's notice that no copy is written.
findings.refutation_tried: A press of Write the copy now is refused for the same reason before it reads (case-copy.mjs:168-175), so there is no other road to the read; reading an existing file would expose nothing more than the file already does. Whether not reading is meant (a copy a player may have rewritten is not trusted) is not said in the paper or the code: FILES_UPLOAD would let a player overwrite a file only with its name known.

superseded_by: Within the stage: the passphrase design (e1afdd84, 6116f17d; R7340-R7344) was taken out by 18df17c4 on the owner's word of 14.11.2026 before release
